## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
You need to fix one rule violation: Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 attempts. The 8-attempt loop in `fetch_inventory` breaks the project's rule limiting retries to 3. That rule applies here because the exemption the pull request adds to `docs/review-rules.md` is part of the change under review, not existing policy.

## Changes
This pull request adds `fetch_inventory`, a legacy inventory fetcher that tries up to 8 times, and `probe`, an inventory health probe that tries up to 3 times. Both raise HTTP errors at once and retry other `OSError`s. It also adds parametrized tests for both and a line in `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 attempts — When the legacy service is down, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts: `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8`. This breaks docs/review-rules.md:5, which AGENTS.md:3 makes binding: "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." The exemption added at docs/review-rules.md:7 is part of this change, so it cannot authorize the loop. — When the upstream is down, each call can hold a worker thread for about 87 seconds (8 × 10 s timeout plus 7 × 1 s delay), which is the stall the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` and update the `8` in `tests/test_retries.py:10`, or get the exemption approved as its own policy change before relying on it.
